title: Why normal cells stop and cancer cells don't
body: Your body makes new cells by dividing, when it needs them.
Cells send messages to each other. They stop dividing when growth or healing is complete.
Cancer cells ignore the signals that tell cells to stop dividing.
So cancer cells keep doubling. They can form a lump called a tumour.
This starts from changes to genes that control how cells grow and divide.
realWorld: A cut heals because cells divide to replace damaged ones. Then they stop when healing is complete.
model: This is a teaching model. Real cells are far smaller and more complicated; the dishes show the idea.
